decisions.statement: The category rules and the item rules and the buy rules have one act set.
An act that writes takes the store it writes through rather than reaching it.
The act naming no store takes the store and hands it to the act that writes.
A write is named on the caller's list as soon as that write has gone through.
An act that wrote and then threw names that write in its refusal.
A write the store refused names nothing, because nothing was written.
An act every kind carries is written once here and named by each command.
A call is read, refused or run through one act here rather than by each command.
A command names the act to run and states nothing of how a call is read.
The flags a command takes are read against the list its own page states.
Nothing here leaves the work for a command to open itself.
A command catching what its own seam throws is written without this act.
Nothing here adds to the reasons the reader gave.
A command whose refusal is built from that list is written without this act.
A field the call names nothing for is left as that field was.
A rule is named by its id rather than by its place in the list.
An id no rule of that kind carries is answered as the data rather than as the call.
A locked rule refuses the acts that change that rule until the call says to force those acts.
Locking and unlocking sit in front of no guard of their own.
A clone is inactive and unlocked whatever its source was.
A clone sits immediately after its source.
A category rule is shown from the written rules first and the derived ones second.
A row says the columns that rule kind carries.
JSON says the whole shape the rule carries.
A fault thrown by the act this calls is answered with that fault's words.
A fault with a code of its own is answered under that code.
An item rule or buy rule write is worked out and then refused, since only a rule is a page yet.
A category rule write lands as page files, since a category rule is a page already.
The rule store this module reads through is in akasha.
The web fields win in a write and lose in a change, by the order they are spread.
Nothing here prints.
Nothing here changes a controlled rule.

definition: what the commands over a temper player's inventory rules read and do alike
